name: Horseshoe (flap) retinal tear
def: A full-thickness retinal break with a flap of retina still attached to vitreous at its anterior margin, produced by vitreoretinal traction (usually during posterior vitreous detachment) at the posterior border of the vitreous base or at a focal vitreoretinal adhesion.
where: Most occur in the equatorial zone at the posterior border of the vitreous base (juxtabasal), between equator and ora; autopsy series show all quadrants, clinically superior/temporal quadrants predominate; frequently at margins of lattice or cystic tufts.
how: Draw a U/horseshoe-shaped area filled red with a blue outline, rounded apex pointing posteriorly (toward the disc) and open horns pointing anteriorly toward the ora; draw the anterior flap as a curved blue line at the base. Add surrounding blue if subretinal fluid is present.
src: CMS L33567 App A (full-thickness break: blue outline filled red); Documentation & Drawing in Ophthalmology (eOphtha) https://www.eophtha.com/posts/documentation-drawing-in-ophthalmology (rolled flap edges as curved blue lines)

name: Operculated retinal hole (round hole with free operculum)
def: A round full-thickness retinal break whose plug of retina (operculum) has been completely avulsed by vitreous traction and floats free in the vitreous above the hole, relieving traction on the hole margin.
where: Between equator and ora; operculum lies in the detached vitreous just anterior to (in front of) the hole; extrabasal holes may arise from avulsed cystic tufts.
how: Draw a small round red-filled circle with a blue outline; draw the free operculum as a small green-filled shape just beside the hole (displaced slightly toward the centre of the chart to indicate it floats in the vitreous).
src: CMS L33567 App A (full-thickness break); Documentation & Drawing in Ophthalmology (eOphtha) https://www.eophtha.com/posts/documentation-drawing-in-ophthalmology (retinal operculum drawn green)

name: Atrophic round hole
def: A small round full-thickness retinal break of trophic (atrophic) origin without a flap or operculum, most often arising within lattice degeneration and not caused by acute vitreous traction.
where: Between equator and ora, frequently within or at the edge of lattice degeneration; primary (non-lattice) holes are usually single, within the vitreous base zone, in elderly eyes.
how: Draw a small round circle filled red with a blue outline; if inside lattice, place it within the lattice band. Surround with a blue ring if a cuff of subretinal fluid is present.

name: Giant retinal tear
def: A full-thickness neurosensory retinal break extending circumferentially for 90° (3 clock hours) or more in the presence of a posteriorly detached vitreous.
where: Circumferential, at or just posterior to the posterior border of the vitreous base (between ora and equator); the posterior retinal flap may fold over (invert) when detached. Associated with high myopia, trauma, Stickler syndrome.
how: Draw a circumferential crescent filled red with a blue outline spanning ≥3 clock hours between equator and ora; draw the posterior flap edge as a curved blue line (folded/inverted edge drawn as a double blue line). Detached retina posterior to it is filled blue.
src: CMS L33567 App A (full-thickness break); note: Documentation & Drawing in Ophthalmology (eOphtha) https://www.eophtha.com/posts/documentation-drawing-in-ophthalmology alternatively cross-lines the open area in red, but CMS reserves red cross-hatch for partial-thickness breaks

def: A foveal lesion with interruption of all neural retinal layers from the internal limiting membrane to the retinal pigment epithelium, seen ophthalmoscopically as a round red punched-out defect often with a grey cuff of subretinal fluid and sometimes an overlying (pseudo)operculum.
where: Centred on the fovea; cuff of subretinal fluid around the hole; yellow deposits may be seen at the base; prehole opacity/(pseudo)operculum may lie on the posterior hyaloid.

name: Partial-thickness retinal break
def: A retinal break that involves only part of the neurosensory retinal thickness (e.g., inner-layer hole of retinoschisis, lamellar hole, deep erosion), so that no direct communication exists between vitreous and subretinal space.
where: Most often peripheral (within lattice, at the vitreous base or in the inner wall of retinoschisis); at the fovea it is charted as a lamellar macular hole.

name: Inner-layer hole in retinoschisis
def: A break confined to the thin inner wall of a retinoschisis cavity; small and round in degenerative retinoschisis, but may be very large in X-linked retinoschisis, leaving vessels bridging the defect.

name: Lattice degeneration
def: A circumferentially oriented, sharply demarcated spindle-shaped area of peripheral retinal thinning with overlying vitreous liquefaction and firm vitreoretinal adhesion at its margins, often showing white sclerotic vessels, pigment and small atrophic holes.

name: Typical degenerative (senile) retinoschisis
def: Splitting of the peripheral neurosensory retina at the outer plexiform layer, arising from confluent typical cystoid degeneration, forming a smooth, immobile, shallow dome with a thin transparent inner wall, often with white flecks (snowflakes) and sheathed vessels.
where: Bilateral and symmetric in many patients, inferotemporal most often, then superotemporal; extends from the ora posteriorly, posterior border frequently post-equatorial; produces an absolute scotoma.

def: Splitting of the peripheral retina at the nerve fibre layer, arising from reticular cystoid degeneration, forming a more elevated, bullous cavity with an extremely thin inner wall and a higher frequency of large outer-layer breaks.
where: Inferotemporal most often; may extend posterior to the equator; outer-layer holes are typically large, round and posterior.

def: A retinal detachment arising when schisis fluid passes through outer-layer breaks into the subretinal space, either localized and stable or progressive and symptomatic when combined with inner-layer breaks.

name: Rhegmatogenous retinal detachment
def: Separation of the neurosensory retina from the retinal pigment epithelium caused by liquefied vitreous passing through one or more full-thickness retinal breaks into the subretinal space; a fresh detachment is convex, corrugated and mobile.
where: Starts at the causative peripheral break (most often a superior or temporal horseshoe tear) and spreads from the ora posteriorly; record extent in clock hours and macula on/off status.
size: 1 clock hour to total (12 clock hours)
how: Shade the detached area solid blue inside a blue boundary; draw the causative break within it as a blue outline filled red, and a black scalloped line on the ora circle wherever the detachment reaches the ora.

name: Subclinical (localized) retinal detachment
def: Asymptomatic, localized retinal detachment surrounding a peripheral retinal break, with subretinal fluid confined to the periphery and no symptomatic field loss; it rarely progresses and may regress spontaneously.

size: a few disc diameters around the break; 1–2 clock hours
how: Small blue-shaded area around the break (break drawn as a blue outline filled red); add a black line on its posterior border if a pigmented demarcation line is present.

def: Retinal detachment without a retinal break, caused by subretinal accumulation of exudate when inflammatory, infectious, neoplastic, vascular or choroidal disease breaks down the blood–retinal barrier; the retina is smooth and convex and the fluid shifts with posture.

def: Collection of serous fluid in the suprachoroidal space that produces smooth, dome-shaped, brownish elevations of the choroid and overlying retina, usually peripheral and often associated with hypotony.

def: Ring-shaped condensation of peripapillary glial tissue torn from the optic disc margin and suspended in the posterior hyaloid, the classic sign of complete posterior vitreous detachment.
where: Floats in the vitreous in front of the optic disc and moves with eye movement.
how: Small green ring drawn over or just in front of the optic disc.

name: Vitreous hemorrhage
def: Extravasated blood within the vitreous gel or retrohyaloid space, most often from proliferative diabetic retinopathy, a retinal tear, neovascularization after vein occlusion, or PVD without a tear.
where: Diffuse or localized; older blood settles inferiorly and dehemoglobinizes to yellow-white; record density and the area of fundus obscured.
how: Shade the area of fundus obscured by hemorrhage green (lighter shading for less dense hemorrhage).

name: Red blood in vitreous (fresh clot)
def: Fresh, red (not yet dehemoglobinized) blood or clot visible in the vitreous cavity, distinguished on the chart from older dispersed vitreous hemorrhage.
where: Over the bleeding source (tear, neovascular frond) or as a clot in the vitreous, often inferior.
size: small clot to several clock hours
how: Green outline filled red over the clot or fresh blood.
src: CMS L33567 App A

name: Subhyaloid / preretinal hemorrhage
def: Blood trapped between the posterior hyaloid (or ILM) and the retina, forming a dark red, sharply bounded, often boat-shaped collection with a flat upper fluid level that hides the underlying retina.
where: Premacular or along the arcades/neovascular fronds; red cells settle inferiorly to give a horizontal upper meniscus (D shape).
size: 1–8 disc diameters (mean ~6 DD in a YAG hyaloidotomy series)
how: Solid red D-shaped area with a straight horizontal upper border.
src: Documentation & Drawing in Ophthalmology (eOphtha): red solid = 'Haemorrhages (pre-retinal and intra-retinal)' https://www.eophtha.com/posts/documentation-drawing-in-ophthalmology; CMS L33567 App A red = hemorrhages

name: Vitreous membrane / vitreoretinal traction band
def: Condensed or fibrotic sheet or strand of vitreous that inserts on the retina and transmits traction, seen as a grey-white membrane crossing the vitreous cavity.
where: Draw its course through the vitreous to its retinal insertion (tear flap, lattice, neovascular frond, macula, disc).
size: variable; may span the posterior pole to the periphery
how: Solid green line(s) or sheet outline ending at the retinal insertion; add an arrow for the direction of traction.
src: Documentation & Drawing in Ophthalmology (eOphtha): green solid = 'Vitreous membranes' https://www.eophtha.com/posts/documentation-drawing-in-ophthalmology; Jayanna & Shanmugam 2022 (PMID 36190076)

name: Fibrovascular proliferation (fibrovascular membrane)
def: Neovascular fronds with accompanying fibrous tissue growing from the disc or retina onto the posterior hyaloid (e.g., in proliferative diabetic retinopathy), whose contraction causes vitreous hemorrhage and tractional detachment.
where: Along the major vascular arcades and on the optic disc, often with broad plaque-like adhesions at several sites.
size: 1/4 disc diameter to several clock hours along the arcades
how: Orange-filled (elevated neovascularization) frond with a green outline for its elevated fibrous component; involuted, purely fibrous tissue drawn in green only.

name: Asteroid hyalosis
def: Numerous small white-to-cream spherical calcium-phosphate (hydroxyapatite) bodies suspended in and moving with the vitreous gel, usually unilateral and asymptomatic.
where: Diffusely distributed in the gel; bodies move with the vitreous and return to position rather than settling; can obscure the fundus view.
how: Green stippled area over the part of the fundus obscured.
src: Documentation & Drawing in Ophthalmology (eOphtha): green stippled = asteroid hyalosis https://www.eophtha.com/posts/documentation-drawing-in-ophthalmology; Jayanna & Shanmugam 2022 (PMID 36190076)

name: Synchysis scintillans (cholesterolosis bulbi)
def: Refractile golden cholesterol crystals floating freely in liquefied vitreous that settle inferiorly when the eye is still, typically after long-standing vitreous hemorrhage, trauma, chronic inflammation or chronic retinal detachment.
where: Swirl up with eye movement, then sink to the inferior vitreous cavity.
how: Scattered green dots concentrated over the inferior fundus; label to distinguish from asteroid hyalosis.
src: CMS L33567 App A (green = opacities in media); dot pattern inferred to distinguish from asteroid hyalosis

name: Vitreous cells / haze (vitritis)
def: Inflammatory cells, protein or pigment clumps in the vitreous that reduce the clarity of the fundus view, graded clinically on the standardized (SUN) vitreous haze scale.
where: Diffuse or localized over an inflammatory focus; record the grade (0–4+).
how: Green stippling over the hazy area, denser for higher grades; annotate the haze grade.
src: CMS L33567 App A (green = opacities in media)

name: Intraocular foreign body
def: Retained foreign material that has penetrated the globe and lies in the vitreous cavity or is embedded in the retina/choroid, often with vitreous hemorrhage and a retinal impact site.
where: Free in the vitreous (often inferior) or impacted on the posterior retina; draw the entry track and retinal impact site.
size: <1 to several mm (draw to scale against the disc)
how: Solid green shape at the foreign-body position; mark its track as a green line and the retinal impact site (red hemorrhage, blue-outlined red break).
src: Documentation & Drawing in Ophthalmology (eOphtha): green solid = 'IOFB' https://www.eophtha.com/posts/documentation-drawing-in-ophthalmology; Jayanna & Shanmugam 2022 (PMID 36190076)

name: Retained (dropped) lens fragment
def: Nuclear, epinuclear or cortical lens material dislocated into the vitreous cavity during cataract surgery, often lying on the inferior retina with intraocular inflammation and raised pressure.
where: Usually rests on the inferior retina or posterior pole, sometimes enveloped by vitreous.
how: Green-outlined, green cross-hatched opacity at its position; label 'nucleus' or 'cortex'.
src: CMS L33567 App A (green = opacities in media); cross-hatching inferred to distinguish from IOFB

name: Encircling scleral buckle (band)
def: Silicone band sutured 360° around the globe beneath the rectus muscles, indenting the sclera to support the vitreous base and retinal breaks and relieve circumferential traction.
where: Circumferential 360° ridge typically at or just anterior to the equator; segmental elements may be added beneath breaks.
how: Two parallel circumferential lines around the equator marking the buckle edges: black where the retina is attached, brown where the buckle lies under detached retina.
src: Documentation & Drawing in Ophthalmology (eOphtha): black = 'Edge of buckle beneath the attached retina', brown = 'Edge of buckle beneath the detached retina' https://www.eophtha.com/posts/documentation-drawing-in-ophthalmology

name: Segmental (circumferential) scleral buckle
def: Silicone sponge or solid tire sutured limbus-parallel over a limited arc to indent the sclera beneath one or more retinal breaks.
where: Over the clock hours of the breaks, extending beyond them on each side, usually between the equator and ora; may be combined with vitrectomy for inferior breaks.
how: Two parallel circumferential lines over the involved clock hours with closed ends: black under attached retina, brown under detached retina.

name: Radial sponge (meridional buckle)
def: Sponge explant sutured perpendicular to the limbus (meridionally) beneath a large horseshoe tear to close it while avoiding fishmouthing and radial folds.
where: Radially oriented beneath the tear, from near the ora extending posterior to the tear's posterior edge.
size: about 1 clock hour wide; 2–4 disc diameters long
how: Two parallel radial lines beneath the tear with a closed posterior end: black under attached retina, brown under detached retina.

name: Fishmouthing / radial fold on buckle
def: Radial retinal fold arising from redundant retina over a circumferential buckle that holds a tear open ('fishmouthing') and can leak, typically with large horseshoe tears on limbus-parallel buckles.
where: Runs radially across the circumferential buckle, posteriorly from the gaping tear.
how: Short blue radial lines across the buckle for the fold; the open tear drawn as a blue outline filled red, gaping at its posterior lip.
src: CMS L33567 App A (short blue lines = meridional folds; blue outline filled red = full-thickness break)

name: Scleral buckle intrusion
def: Late erosion of a scleral buckle element through the sclera and choroid into the eye, seen as a smooth grey-white element beneath or through the retina at the buckle site.
where: At the buckle site; may be an incidental finding decades after surgery.
how: Black-outlined segment of the buckle filled white where the element is visible intraocularly.
src: inferred: buckle edge black (Documentation & Drawing in Ophthalmology, eOphtha https://www.eophtha.com/posts/documentation-drawing-in-ophthalmology); white fill for exposed implant

name: Laser retinopexy around a break
def: Two to three rows of confluent photocoagulation burns surrounding a retinal break (and any cuff of fluid) to create a chorioretinal adhesion; healed burns become pigmented scars with atrophic centres.
where: Encircles the break on attached retina; anteriorly the rows may be carried to the ora.
size: ring 1–2 disc diameters wider than the break
how: Rows of small black dots (healed, pigmented burns) encircling the break; draw fresh burns in yellow.
src: Documentation & Drawing in Ophthalmology (eOphtha): black solid = 'Hyperpigmentation as a result of the previous treatment with Cryo/PHC/Diathermy' https://www.eophtha.com/posts/documentation-drawing-in-ophthalmology

name: Laser demarcation (barrier) line
def: Two to three confluent rows of photocoagulation placed on attached retina along the posterior border of a localized detachment to limit its posterior spread.
where: Curved line posterior to the detachment margin on attached retina, with both ends carried to the ora.
how: Curved band of 2–3 rows of black dots on attached retina just posterior to the blue detachment, ends reaching the ora.

name: 360° peripheral laser retinopexy
def: Confluent rows of photocoagulation applied circumferentially around the whole peripheral retina, usually anterior to the equator, as prophylaxis against (re)detachment after vitrectomy or before silicone oil removal.
where: 360° band between the equator and ora.
how: Continuous circumferential band of black dots between the equator and ora circles.

name: Panretinal photocoagulation (PRP) scars
def: Scatter laser burns placed across the mid- and peripheral retina outside the vascular arcades for proliferative ischemic retinopathy, healing as pigmented chorioretinal scars that can enlarge over time.
where: Outside the arcades and nasal to the disc, sparing the macula and papillomacular bundle, out to and beyond the equator; sectoral PRP is limited to an ischemic sector.
how: Scattered black dots filling the mid-periphery outside the arcades, leaving the posterior pole clear.

name: Focal / grid macular laser scars
def: Small laser burns applied to leaking microaneurysms (focal) or in a grid over thickened macula for diabetic macular edema, sparing the foveal centre; healed burns appear as small pigmented or atrophic spots.
where: Within the arcades, sparing the foveal centre; scars may enlarge with time.
size: small spots over a 1–3 disc diameter area
how: Small black dots in the treated macular area, leaving the fovea clear.

name: Fresh laser (photocoagulation) burns
def: Recently applied laser burns visible as grey-white spots of outer-retinal whitening and edema that later pigment into scars.
where: Wherever treatment was applied at this visit; redraw as black scars at follow-up.
size: spots ~100–500 µm in rows or scatter
how: Yellow dots/rows at the treated positions to show fresh, edematous burns.

name: Cryopexy (cryotherapy) scar

where: Around peripheral breaks, often on the buckle; applications are contiguous around the break.
size: each application about 1–2 disc diameters; confluent around the break
how: Black-outlined patches with black stippled pigment around the break; fresh cryo (white frost) may be drawn yellow.

name: External subretinal fluid drainage site
def: Site of transscleral choroidotomy used to drain subretinal fluid during buckling surgery, later visible as a small pigmented chorioretinal scar, sometimes with local subretinal hemorrhage or retinal incarceration.
where: Beneath or beside the buckle where subretinal fluid was deepest, usually between rectus muscles.
how: Small black X at the drainage site; add red if subretinal hemorrhage is present.

name: Drainage retinotomy
def: Small iatrogenic full-thickness retinal opening made during vitrectomy to drain subretinal fluid, usually surrounded by endolaser and visible postoperatively as a round hole within a pigmented laser ring.
where: Usually in the mid-periphery away from the macula, in an area of deep subretinal fluid.
how: Small full-thickness break (blue outline filled red) surrounded by a ring of black laser dots.

name: Relaxing retinotomy / retinectomy edge
def: Surgical incision or excision of contracted, shortened retina (usually peripheral and circumferential) to relieve PVR traction, leaving a free posterior retinal edge secured with endolaser and bare RPE/choroid anteriorly.
where: Most often inferior, 90–180° (up to 360°), anterior to the equator; the posterior edge can fold or slip.
how: Blue line marking the retinectomy edge, the area anterior to it treated as a giant break (blue outline filled red), and 2–3 rows of black laser dots just posterior to the edge.

name: Intraocular gas bubble (air / SF6 / C3F8)
def: Intravitreal air or expansile gas (SF6, C2F6, C3F8) used as internal tamponade after vitrectomy or pneumatic retinopexy, seen as a mobile superior bubble with a horizontal inferior meniscus.
where: Rises to the highest point of the cavity; record % fill and meniscus level; positioning places it against the break.
how: Green outline of the bubble over the superior fundus bounded by a straight horizontal meniscus line; annotate gas type and % fill.

name: Pneumatic retinopexy
def: Office repair combining intravitreal expansile gas injection with cryopexy or laser to the break(s) and head positioning so the bubble tamponades the break, classically for breaks within the superior 8 clock hours.
where: Classic indication: single break or group of breaks no larger than 1 clock hour in the superior 8 clock hours; the bubble is positioned over the break.
size: break(s) ≤1 clock hour; bubble occupies the superior cavity
how: Superior gas bubble outlined green with retinopexy marks around the break (black dots or stipple, yellow if fresh); note any new breaks and dependent demarcation line.
src: inferred: tamponade drawn green (see intraocular gas bubble; PMID 36190076) + Documentation & Drawing in Ophthalmology (eOphtha) black treatment scars https://www.eophtha.com/posts/documentation-drawing-in-ophthalmology

name: Silicone oil tamponade
def: Long-term intravitreal tamponade with silicone oil (lighter or heavier than water) after vitrectomy for complex detachments, showing a glistening reflex at its meniscus and usually requiring later removal.
where: Fills most of the cavity; standard oil floats (inferior aqueous rim), heavy oil sinks (superior aqueous rim); mark under-fill and any oil-retina interface.
how: Green outline of the oil bubble with light green parallel hatching; mark the meniscus (inferior for standard oil, superior for heavy oil) and label 'SO'.
src: inferred: no established colour for silicone oil (Jayanna & Shanmugam 2022, PMID 36190076, https://doi.org/10.4103/ijo.IJO_1004_22); green for vitreous-cavity contents per CMS L33567 App A; hatching distinguishes oil from gas

name: Emulsified silicone oil droplets
def: Dispersion of silicone oil into small droplets after prolonged tamponade, seen as tiny refractile bubbles in the vitreous cavity (and as an inverted pseudohypopyon in the anterior chamber) that may adhere to the retina.
where: Droplets of standard oil gather superiorly in the cavity and on the retinal surface.
size: droplets far smaller than the disc, often diffuse
how: Clusters of small green dots/circles where droplets are seen, mainly superiorly.
src: inferred: tamponade/vitreous contents drawn green (CMS L33567 App A opacities in media; PMID 36190076)

name: Retained perfluorocarbon liquid (PFCL) droplet
def: Residual droplet(s) of heavy perfluorocarbon liquid left after vitrectomy, seen as clear, round, highly refractile bubbles that sink to the dependent vitreous cavity or become trapped subretinally, often beneath the fovea.
where: Preretinal droplets lie in the most dependent cavity; subretinal droplets sit under the posterior pole/fovea and can migrate.
how: Small round green-outlined circle(s) at the droplet position; label 'PFCL' and 'subretinal' when beneath the retina.

name: Postoperative retinal (macular) fold
def: Fold of the reattached retina, sometimes crossing the macula, caused by residual subretinal fluid displaced by gas tamponade or by retinal slippage after detachment repair.
where: Usually across the posterior pole/macula after gas tamponade; can be associated with macular translocation, diplopia and metamorphopsia; may flatten spontaneously.
how: Blue line along the course of the fold on attached retina.

name: Flame / splinter intraretinal hemorrhage
def: A superficial intraretinal hemorrhage in the retinal nerve fibre layer whose feathered, elongated (flame or splinter) shape follows the radial course of the nerve fibres.
where: Peripapillary and along the arcades where the nerve fibre layer is thickest; splinter hemorrhages may sit on the disc margin; oriented radially toward the disc.
how: Solid red short feathered strokes oriented along the nerve-fibre direction (radial to the disc); draw one stroke per hemorrhage or a cluster for many.

name: Dot-blot intraretinal hemorrhage
def: A round, sharply bordered intraretinal hemorrhage in the deeper (inner nuclear/outer plexiform) retinal layers whose compact shape reflects the vertically oriented tissue in those layers.
where: Posterior pole and midperiphery; in diabetic retinopathy most frequent temporal to the macula; counted per quadrant for severity grading (4-2-1 rule).
how: Solid red round dots (dot hemorrhages) and slightly larger irregular red blots placed in the quadrant where seen.

def: Blood trapped between the internal limiting membrane or posterior hyaloid and the retina, typically forming a dense, sharply demarcated boat-shaped pool with a flat upper fluid level that obscures underlying retinal vessels.

where: Centred on the macula in nAMD/PCV; around the source lesion for macroaneurysm or choroidal rupture; may extend beyond the arcades.

name: Roth spot (white-centred hemorrhage)
def: An intraretinal hemorrhage with a pale white or yellow-white centre (fibrin-platelet plug), a non-specific sign seen in endocarditis, leukaemia, anaemia and other systemic disorders.
where: Posterior pole and peripapillary retina, usually multiple and bilateral.

name: Microaneurysm
def: A focal saccular dilation of a retinal capillary wall (from pericyte loss and endothelial proliferation) seen as a tiny, sharply defined red dot; the earliest clinical sign of diabetic retinopathy.
where: Diffuse around the posterior pole, often temporal to the fovea and at the edges of capillary non-perfusion; ring of exudate may surround a leaking cluster.
size: pinpoint, <125 µm (smaller than vein width at disc margin)
how: Very small solid red dots (smaller than dot hemorrhages) stippled over the involved area.

def: Well-demarcated, waxy yellow deposits of lipid and lipoprotein in the outer plexiform layer from chronic leakage of abnormal retinal vessels, ranging from punctate specks to confluent plaques.

def: A partial or complete ring of hard exudates surrounding a focal leaking source (microaneurysm cluster, telangiectasia or macroaneurysm), marking the border between oedematous and normal retina.
where: Posterior pole/macula, centred on the leaking lesion; may straddle the fovea.

name: Macular star (star figure exudate)
def: Hard exudates arranged radially in Henle's fibre layer around the fovea, forming a complete or partial star, classically with optic disc oedema in neuroretinitis or with severe hypertensive retinopathy.
where: Centred on the fovea; a partial (nasal) hemi-star is common; may appear 1–2 weeks after disc oedema.

name: Cotton-wool spot
def: A fluffy, white, ill-defined superficial retinal opacity caused by accumulation of axoplasmic debris in the nerve fibre layer after interruption of axoplasmic transport by focal arteriolar occlusion (ischaemia).
where: Within about 3 DD of the disc in the territory of the radial peripapillary capillaries and along the arcades; overlies vessels.
how: Small fluffy cloud with a soft yellow outline and white centre, drawn over the vessel; keep separate from solid yellow hard exudate dots. (Some charts use green for cotton-wool spots.)

name: Macular edema / retinal thickening
def: Biomicroscopically visible thickening of the macular retina from intraretinal fluid accumulation, graded by its distance from the foveal centre (centre-involving or not) and often accompanied by hard exudates.
where: Within the arcades; note whether it involves the centre, lies within 500 µm of the centre, or covers ≥1 disc area within 1 DD of the centre.

name: Cystoid macular edema
def: Macular oedema in which fluid collects in perifoveal intraretinal cystic spaces arranged radially, giving a honeycomb or petaloid appearance with loss of the foveal reflex.
where: Centred on the fovea; causes include post-cataract surgery (Irvine-Gass), uveitis, diabetes and vein occlusion.
how: Yellow petaloid rosette of small loculi drawn around the fovea.

name: Neovascularization elsewhere (NVE) – flat
def: New retinal vessels arising from retinal veins more than 1 disc diameter from the disc that lie flat on the retinal surface, not yet elevated into the vitreous, typically at the border of perfused and non-perfused retina.
where: Along the major arcades and midperiphery adjacent to capillary non-perfusion; size recorded in disc areas (≥1/2 DA is high-risk in PDR).

def: Retinal new vessels that have grown forward along the posterior hyaloid into the vitreous cavity, often with accompanying fibrous tissue, bleeding into the vitreous when the hyaloid contracts.
where: Arcades/midperiphery at sites of vitreoretinal adhesion; often associated with preretinal or vitreous hemorrhage.

name: Neovascularization of the disc (NVD)
def: New vessels on the optic disc or within 1 disc diameter of its margin, an ischaemic proliferative sign (diabetes, ischaemic CRVO, ocular ischaemia) whose size is graded against standard photographs.
where: On the disc surface or within 1 DD of the margin; ≥1/4–1/3 disc area defines high-risk PDR.

name: Intraretinal microvascular abnormalities (IRMA)
def: Tortuous, dilated intraretinal vessel segments (shunts or early intraretinal new vessels) adjacent to areas of capillary non-perfusion that do not breach the internal limiting membrane, a marker of severe non-proliferative diabetic retinopathy.
where: Posterior pole and midperiphery bordering non-perfused retina; graded per quadrant.
how: Short, irregular, kinked red lines lying within the retina (not raised), drawn between arteriole and venule in the quadrant seen.

name: Venous beading
def: Localized alternating dilation and constriction of a retinal vein giving a string-of-beads appearance, a sign of severe retinal ischaemia in diabetic retinopathy.
where: Mainly between the first and third venous bifurcations; graded by number of quadrants (≥2 quadrants = severe NPDR by 4-2-1 rule).

name: Branch retinal vein occlusion (BRVO)
def: Occlusion of a branch retinal vein, usually at an arteriovenous crossing, producing a sectoral, apex-to-crossing wedge of flame and dot-blot hemorrhages, dilated tortuous vein, cotton-wool spots and macular oedema in the drained territory.
where: Wedge with apex at the occluding AV crossing, fanning toward the periphery; superotemporal most common, then inferotemporal; macular branch occlusions are limited to the macula.
how: Draw the affected vein dilated and tortuous in blue, fill its territory with red flame/blot hemorrhages, mark the occlusion site at the AV crossing in brown, and add yellow for oedema/exudate and cotton-wool spots.

name: Hemiretinal (hemicentral) vein occlusion
def: Occlusion of one of the two trunks of a dual-trunked central retinal vein at or near the disc, causing CRVO-type hemorrhages confined to the superior or inferior half of the retina.
where: Respects the horizontal raphe; occlusion site at or behind the disc rather than at an AV crossing.
how: Red hemorrhages throughout one hemifundus up to the periphery with the corresponding dilated blue vein trunk; mark the occlusion at the disc in brown.
src: CMS L33567 App A

name: Central retinal vein occlusion (CRVO)
def: Occlusion of the central retinal vein at or behind the lamina cribrosa producing dilated tortuous veins and hemorrhages in all four quadrants, with disc oedema, cotton-wool spots and macular oedema, classified as non-ischaemic or ischaemic.
where: Hemorrhages extend from disc to periphery; peripheral hemorrhage severity relates to anterior-segment neovascular risk.
how: All veins drawn dilated and tortuous in blue, red flame/blot hemorrhages in every quadrant, yellow cotton-wool spots/oedema, swollen disc margin, occlusion marked brown at the disc.

name: Branch retinal artery occlusion (BRAO)
def: Occlusion of a branch retinal artery, usually embolic at a bifurcation, causing acute opaque whitening (inner retinal infarction) of the retina in the territory supplied distal to the block.
where: Wedge of whitening distal to the occlusion, usually temporal arcade branches; embolus often visible at the proximal bifurcation; whitening resolves over weeks leaving attenuated, sometimes sheathed arterioles.
size: 1–3 clock hours / one sector of the posterior pole
how: Shade the whitened retinal sector yellow (intraretinal oedema) along the course of the affected red arteriole and mark the occluded segment or embolus in brown.

name: Central retinal artery occlusion (CRAO)
def: Occlusion of the central retinal artery producing diffuse whitening of the posterior-pole inner retina with a cherry-red spot at the fovea, attenuated arterioles and sometimes segmented (box-car) blood columns.
where: Whitening most marked in the posterior pole where the ganglion cell layer is thickest; a patent cilioretinal artery spares a tongue of retina between disc and fovea.
size: whole posterior pole within the arcades
how: Shade the posterior pole yellow (ischaemic oedema), leave a red dot at the fovea (cherry-red spot), draw arteries thin in red with interrupted segments, and mark the occlusion at the disc in brown; leave any cilioretinal-spared tongue unshaded.

name: Cilioretinal artery occlusion
def: Occlusion of a cilioretinal artery (arising from the posterior ciliary circulation at the disc margin) producing a tongue-shaped zone of retinal whitening between the temporal disc and the fovea, isolated or with CRVO or arteritic disease.
where: Papillomacular bundle region from the temporal disc margin toward the fovea.
how: Yellow tongue-shaped area of whitening from the temporal disc edge toward the fovea along the cilioretinal vessel (drawn red); mark the vessel origin in brown.

name: Cherry-red spot
def: Relative red appearance of the foveola, where the retina is thin and the choroid shows through, contrasted against surrounding opaque whitened (ischaemic or storage-laden) perifoveal retina.
where: Exactly at the foveola; seen in acute CRAO, ocular ischaemic syndrome and lysosomal storage diseases.

where: Distributed along the territory of the occluded arteriole (sector, cilioretinal tongue or whole posterior pole).

def: Intra-arterial embolic material lodged in a retinal arteriole, classically at a bifurcation: refractile yellow cholesterol (Hollenhorst) plaques, chalky white calcific emboli, or dull grey-white elongated platelet-fibrin emboli.
where: At arteriolar bifurcations or where the vessel narrows, on the disc or along the arcades; may or may not cause distal occlusion.

where: Segmental along veins (periphlebitis) or arteries; midperiphery common in vasculitis; follows former occlusions.

def: Retinal vessels converted to white cords with no visible blood column after chronic occlusion, marking severe non-perfusion (e.g., ischaemic PDR, old BRVO/BRAO, sickle retinopathy).

def: An idiopathic, usually unilateral retinal vasculopathy of young males with telangiectatic and aneurysmal ('light-bulb') retinal vessels and massive intraretinal and subretinal yellow lipid exudation that may progress to exudative retinal detachment.

def: In retinopathy of prematurity, a thin flat white line (stage 1) or a raised, thickened ridge with height and width (stage 2) separating vascularised posterior retina from avascular peripheral retina, recorded by zone and by extent in clock hours.

def: Sharply demarcated, round or lobulated areas of RPE, photoreceptor and choriocapillaris loss through which large choroidal vessels are visible, representing late (atrophic) AMD.
where: Parafoveal first (often foveal-sparing horseshoe), later involving the fovea; multifocal lesions coalesce.
how: Outline each atrophic area in black and cross-hatch in red (chorioretinal atrophy of attached retina); add brown flecks for marginal pigment.
src: inferred: CMS L33567 App A paving-stone (chorioretinal atrophy of attached retina) = black outline cross-hatched red

[Diagnostic approach and treatment paradigm in atrophic age related macular degeneration: Recommendations of the France Macula Federation].

syn: complete rpe and outer retinal atrophy
match: complete rpe and outer retinal atrophy

name: Choroidal / macular neovascularization (CNV/MNV)
def: Neovascular tissue growing from the choroid beneath or through the RPE (type 1, 2) or from the retinal circulation (type 3), seen as a grey-green or yellow-grey subretinal lesion with associated subretinal fluid, hemorrhage, exudate or PED.
where: Subfoveal, juxtafoveal or extrafoveal; also peripapillary, along angioid streaks, lacquer cracks or choroidal ruptures.
how: Purple patch at the membrane location with surrounding blue for subretinal fluid, red for hemorrhage and yellow for exudate.
src: inferred: CMS L33567 App A purple = flat neovascularization (CNV lies beneath the retina, not elevated into vitreous)

refs.title: Consensus Nomenclature for Reporting Neovascular Age-Related Macular Degeneration Data: Consensus on Neovascular Age-Related Macular Degeneration Nomenclature Study Group.

name: Disciform scar (subretinal fibrosis)
def: End-stage fibrous (fibroglial) replacement of a macular neovascular lesion, appearing as an elevated white-yellow subretinal plaque with variable pigmentation and overlying retinal atrophy.
where: Subfoveal or centred on the former neovascular lesion.
how: Yellow (subretinal fibrosis) patch with brown pigment clumps at the margin/within.
src: Indirect ophthalmoscopy and fundus drawing (Dr Sonali Raj Singh, SlideShare teaching deck) https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/indirect-ophthalmoscopy-and-fundus-drawing/238698487

refs.title: Fibrogliosis in neovascular age-related macular degeneration: A new mechanistic perspective.

name: Pigment epithelial detachment (PED)
def: Separation of the RPE from Bruch's membrane by fluid, blood, drusenoid material or fibrovascular tissue, seen as a sharply outlined, dome-shaped orange-yellow elevation.
where: Macula (nAMD, PCV, CSC); may be multiple or peripapillary.
how: Brown round/oval dome with a crisp outline; red notch or fill if hemorrhagic, purple adjacent if vascularized.
src: Documentation & Drawing in Ophthalmology (P. Dutta Majumder, eOphtha) https://www.eophtha.com/posts/documentation-drawing-in-ophthalmology

refs.title: Retinal pigment epithelial detachment: Molecular mechanisms, multimodal imaging classification, and clinical management across the spectrum of macular disease.

name: RPE tear (rip)
def: A rupture of the RPE at the edge of a PED, with retraction and scrolling of the torn RPE into a hyperpigmented ridge beside a sharply defined crescent of bare Bruch's membrane.
where: At the margin of a vascularized PED, spontaneously or after anti-VEGF; graded by size and foveal involvement.
how: Crescent outline in brown with the bare area left unfilled and a thick brown line for the scrolled, pigmented RPE edge.
src: inferred: CMS L33567 App A brown = RPE pigmentation seen through attached retina

refs.title: MANAGEMENT OF RETINAL PIGMENT EPITHELIUM TEAR DURING ANTI-VASCULAR ENDOTHELIAL GROWTH FACTOR THERAPY.
ASSOCIATION BETWEEN RETINAL PIGMENT EPITHELIUM TEAR AND ANTI-VASCULAR ENDOTHELIAL GROWTH FACTOR THERAPY: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.

name: Central serous chorioretinopathy (serous macular detachment)
def: A pachychoroid disorder in which choroidal hyperpermeability and RPE dysfunction cause a well-circumscribed, round serous detachment of the neurosensory macula, often with a small PED or yellow subretinal precipitates.
where: Round/oval detachment centred on or near the fovea; chronic cases leave gravitational descending tracts inferiorly.
how: Blue outlined (and lightly shaded) round area of detached macula; small brown dome for any PED; inferior gravitational tract as a blue/brown band.
src: CMS L33567 App A

refs.title: Central serous chorioretinopathy: Recent findings and new physiopathology hypothesis.
Pachychoroid disease: review and update.

name: Polypoidal choroidal vasculopathy (polyps)
def: A subtype of type 1 macular neovascularization with aneurysmal polypoidal dilations of a branching vascular network beneath the RPE, seen as orange-red subretinal nodules with serosanguineous PEDs and hemorrhage.
where: Macula or peripapillary region.
size: polyps 1/8–1/2 DD; lesion up to several DD
how: Orange round nodules at polyp positions, with brown PEDs, red subretinal hemorrhage and blue subretinal fluid as present.
src: inferred: CMS L33567 App A orange = elevated neovascularization (polyps are elevated aneurysmal neovascular lesions)

refs.title: Polypoidal Choroidal Vasculopathy.

name: Vitelliform lesion (adult-onset foveomacular vitelliform)
def: A round, yellow, slightly elevated subretinal deposit of lipofuscin-laden material between the neurosensory retina and RPE at or near the fovea, often with central pigment.
where: Foveal or perifoveal, usually bilateral and asymmetric.
how: Solid yellow round dome at the fovea; brown central dot for pigment.
src: Documentation & Drawing in Ophthalmology (P. Dutta Majumder, eOphtha) https://www.eophtha.com/posts/documentation-drawing-in-ophthalmology

name: Epiretinal membrane (ERM)
def: A fibrocellular preretinal membrane on the inner retinal surface that produces a glistening cellophane reflex and, when it contracts, radiating retinal striae, vessel tortuosity and macular distortion (pucker).
where: Over the macula, often eccentric; striae radiate toward its contraction centre.
how: Green outline of the membrane with green wavy striae radiating from its centre; draw dragged vessels accordingly.
src: Retinal diagram (Dr Sabin Sahu, SlideShare teaching deck) https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/retinal-diagram-dr-sabin-sahu/57240044

refs.title: Pathophysiology and clinical aspects of epiretinal membrane - review.
Stiffness of retinal and choroidal tissue: a surface wrinkling analysis of epiretinal membranes and choroidal folds.

name: Vitreomacular traction (VMT)
def: Anomalous posterior vitreous detachment with persistent vitreous attachment to the macula that distorts the fovea (pseudocysts, schisis, elevation), classified as focal (≤1500 µm) or broad (>1500 µm).
where: Perifoveal vitreous separated with residual foveal attachment; confirmed on OCT but taut hyaloid may be seen biomicroscopically.
how: Green line/outline of the posterior hyaloid converging onto the fovea at the attachment site; yellow for associated foveal cysts.
src: Documentation & Drawing in Ophthalmology (P. Dutta Majumder, eOphtha) https://www.eophtha.com/posts/documentation-drawing-in-ophthalmology

refs.title: The International Vitreomacular Traction Study Group classification of vitreomacular adhesion, traction, and macular hole.

name: Impending macular hole (Gass stage 1)
def: Loss of the foveal depression with a yellow foveolar spot (stage 1A) or yellow ring (stage 1B) from vitreofoveal traction before a full-thickness defect forms.
where: Exactly at the foveola.
how: Small yellow dot (1A) or yellow ring (1B) at the fovea.
src: inferred: CMS L33567 App A yellow = intraretinal edema/deposit (yellow foveal spot)

refs.title: [Age-dependent idiopathic macular foramen. Current concepts of the pathogenesis, diagnosis, and treatment].
New insights into the pathoanatomy of macular holes based on features of optical coherence tomography.

name: Macular pseudohole
def: A foveal-sparing epiretinal membrane that steepens the foveal pit so that it mimics a hole biomicroscopically, with no loss of foveal tissue.
where: ERM encircles the fovea with a central opening.
how: Intact red fovea surrounded by a green ring (contracted ERM edge).
src: inferred: ERM green per teaching code; intact fovea red per CMS L33567 App A attached retina

refs.title: Optical coherence tomography-based consensus definition for lamellar macular hole.

name: Angioid streaks
def: Irregular, jagged, red-brown to grey linear breaks in a calcified, brittle Bruch's membrane radiating from a peripapillary ring, associated with pseudoxanthoma elasticum, Paget disease and haemoglobinopathies and prone to CNV.
where: Concentric ring around the disc with spokes radiating outward, tapering toward the periphery; may cross the macula.
size: 1–5 disc diameters long, narrower than veins
how: Brown jagged lines radiating from a brown peripapillary ring; add purple for any associated CNV.
src: inferred: CMS L33567 App A brown = choroidal/RPE pigmentation seen through attached retina

refs.title: Comprehensive review of angioid streaks.
Angioid streaks-related choroidal neovascularization: Clinical features, multimodal imaging-based differential diagnosis, and optimized treatment strategies.

name: Lacquer cracks
def: Fine, yellowish-white, irregular linear breaks in Bruch's membrane in the posterior pole of pathologically myopic eyes, a 'plus' lesion predisposing to myopic CNV and subretinal hemorrhage.
where: Posterior pole/macula within a staphyloma, often horizontal or branching; acute cracks may show small subretinal hemorrhage.
how: Thin yellow branching lines at the macula; small red dot for any associated hemorrhage.
src: inferred: no published convention; yellow line chosen for yellow-white Bruch's membrane breaks (cf. CMS L33567 App A yellow = chorioretinal lesion), distinct from brown angioid streaks

refs.title: International photographic classification and grading system for myopic maculopathy.
Insights on Acute and Chronic Lacquer Cracks as Imaged with Visible Light OCT.

name: Posterior staphyloma
def: An outpouching of a circumscribed region of the posterior globe with a radius of curvature smaller than the surrounding eye wall, the hallmark of pathologic myopia.
where: Wide macular, narrow macular, peripapillary, nasal or inferior types; its edge is seen as a curvilinear vessel bend/pigmented line.
size: several disc diameters (often whole posterior pole)
how: Brown curved outline tracing the staphyloma edge around the posterior pole.
src: Documentation & Drawing in Ophthalmology (P. Dutta Majumder, eOphtha) https://www.eophtha.com/posts/documentation-drawing-in-ophthalmology

refs.title: Posterior staphyloma in pathologic myopia.
Understanding Posterior Staphyloma in Pathologic Myopia: Current Overview, New Input, and Perspectives.

name: Myopic chorioretinal atrophy (diffuse / patchy / macular)
def: Degenerative chorioretinal atrophy of pathologic myopia, from ill-defined yellowish diffuse atrophy to sharply demarcated grey-white patchy atrophy exposing sclera and macular atrophy, graded in META-PM categories 2–4.
where: Peripapillary and macular, within the staphyloma.
how: Black outline cross-hatched red for patchy/macular atrophy (dashed outline for diffuse atrophy); brown for marginal pigment.
src: inferred: CMS L33567 App A paving-stone (chorioretinal atrophy of attached retina) = black outline cross-hatched red

refs.title: International photographic classification and grading system for myopic maculopathy.

name: Fuchs spot
def: A round, dark pigmented macular lesion representing RPE hyperplasia over a regressed myopic choroidal neovascular membrane, a 'plus' lesion of pathologic myopia.
where: Foveal or juxtafoveal in highly myopic eyes.
how: Solid brown round spot at the macula.
src: CMS L33567 App A

refs.title: International photographic classification and grading system for myopic maculopathy.

name: Bull's-eye maculopathy
def: A ring of parafoveal RPE depigmentation sparing the central fovea, giving a target appearance, classically in advanced hydroxychloroquine/chloroquine toxicity and some cone dystrophies.
where: Annulus around the fovea (pericentral pattern in Asian patients may lie near the arcades).
how: Brown annulus around a spared red foveal centre.
src: inferred: CMS L33567 App A brown = RPE pigment change seen through attached retina

refs.title: Mimickers of hydroxychloroquine retinal toxicity.
Target in Sight: A Comprehensive Review of Hydroxychloroquine-Induced Bull's Eye Maculopathy.

name: Choroidal (chorioretinal) folds
def: Alternating light and dark parallel undulations of the inner choroid, Bruch's membrane and RPE across the posterior pole, caused by hypotony, orbital mass, scleritis, hyperopia or idiopathically.
where: Usually horizontal or oblique lines across the macula, sometimes concentric around the disc.
how: Brown parallel lines across the involved posterior pole following the fold orientation.
src: inferred: CMS L33567 App A brown = choroidal/RPE change seen through attached retina

refs.title: [Choroidal folds].
Stiffness of retinal and choroidal tissue: a surface wrinkling analysis of epiretinal membranes and choroidal folds.

name: Traumatic choroidal rupture
def: A traumatic break in the choroid, Bruch's membrane and RPE, typically an arc-shaped yellow-white streak concentric to the disc in the posterior pole, often initially hidden by subretinal hemorrhage and later complicated by CNV.
where: Crescentic, concentric to the optic disc, frequently submacular.
how: Yellow crescent concentric to the disc with brown pigmented margins; red subretinal blood if acute; purple if CNV develops.
src: inferred: no published convention; yellow for exposed sclera/atrophy with brown RPE pigment margins (CMS L33567 App A brown)

refs.title: Post-Traumatic Choroidal Rupture: Characteristics, Management and Outcomes.

name: Commotio retinae (Berlin oedema)
def: Transient grey-white opacification of the outer retina after blunt trauma due to photoreceptor outer-segment disruption, at the macula (Berlin oedema) or periphery at the site of impact or contrecoup.
where: Posterior pole (Berlin) or peripheral at the impact site; may be accompanied by choroidal rupture or hemorrhage.
how: Yellow stippled area of whitening; a red foveal dot if a pseudo-cherry-red spot is present.
src: CMS L33567 App A

refs.title: Severe Macular Commotio Retinae Following a Fall from a Horse in a Pediatric Patient.
Commotio Retinae.

name: Elschnig spots / Siegrist streaks (hypertensive choroidopathy)
def: Signs of choroidal ischaemia in malignant hypertension: Elschnig spots are multifocal yellowish RPE lesions over infarcted choriocapillaris lobules that later become pigmented with a pale halo, and Siegrist streaks are linear hyperpigmented lines along sclerosed choroidal arteries.
where: Posterior pole and midperiphery; often with serous retinal detachment and hypertensive retinopathy signs.
how: Acute: yellow spots; healed: brown dots with a pale yellow halo; Siegrist streaks as short brown lines along choroidal vessel courses; any serous detachment in blue.
src: inferred: CMS L33567 App A yellow = chorioretinal lesion (acute) and brown = RPE/choroidal pigmentation (healed)

Hypertensive choroidopathy in atypical hemolytic-uremic syndrome.

name: Optic disc edema
def: Swelling of the optic nerve head from axoplasmic stasis, seen as an elevated, hyperaemic disc with blurred margins and obscuration of vessels at the disc edge, of any cause (e.g. NAION, optic neuritis/papillitis, raised intracranial pressure).
where: Disc and immediately adjacent peripapillary nerve fibre layer; may be sectoral (e.g. altitudinal in NAION).
size: Whole disc (1 DD) plus a 0.25-0.5 DD peripapillary halo
how: Fill the disc circle yellow and feather its margin with short radial yellow strokes into the peripapillary retina to show blurred margins; add peripapillary flame haemorrhages as red strokes if present.
src: inferred: CMS L33567 App A yellow = intraretinal edema; no standard disc-swelling code exists (Jayanna S, Shanmugam PM. It is time for more colors! Indian J Ophthalmol 2022, https://doi.org/10.4103/ijo.IJO_1004_22)

refs.title: Resolution of disc oedema in nonarteritic anterior ischaemic optic neuropathy versus optic neuritis: a retrospective, cross-sectional study.
Optical Coherence Tomography Neuro-Toolbox for the Diagnosis and Management of Papilledema, Optic Disc Edema, and Pseudopapilledema.

name: Papilledema
def: Optic disc swelling secondary to raised intracranial pressure, usually bilateral, with visual function typically preserved in the acute phase.
where: Both discs; may be accompanied by peripapillary haemorrhages, cotton-wool spots and peripapillary retinal/choroidal folds.
size: Whole disc plus peripapillary halo, up to about 1 DD beyond the margin in severe cases
how: Draw on both eye charts: fill each disc yellow with feathered radial yellow margins; add red flame haemorrhages and yellow cotton-wool spots around the disc where seen.
src: inferred: CMS L33567 App A yellow = intraretinal edema; red = retinal hemorrhages

refs.title: Papilledema: A review of etiology, pathophysiology, diagnosis, and management.
Anemia and papilledema.

name: Optic disc pallor / optic atrophy
def: Loss of the normal pink colour of the neuroretinal rim from loss of retinal ganglion cell axons, diffuse or sectoral (e.g. temporal pallor from papillomacular bundle loss).
where: Whole disc or a sector of the rim; temporal sector in papillomacular bundle disease.
size: Whole disc or a sector of it (1 DD)
how: Outline the disc in black and leave the pale area white, shading only the affected sector for sectoral pallor; annotate the sector (e.g. 'temporal pallor').
src: inferred: natural-colour depiction; no standard code exists for disc pallor (Jayanna S, Shanmugam PM. Indian J Ophthalmol 2022, https://doi.org/10.4103/ijo.IJO_1004_22)

refs.title: Pediatric Optic Disc Pallor.
Dominant optic atrophy: updates on the pathophysiology and clinical manifestations of the optic atrophy 1 mutation.

name: Glaucomatous optic disc cupping
def: Enlargement and deepening of the optic cup with diffuse or focal thinning (notching) of the neuroretinal rim from glaucomatous axon loss, often with vertical elongation of the cup.
clock: superior and inferior poles of the disc
where: Rim loss characteristically at the inferotemporal and superotemporal poles; record the vertical cup-to-disc ratio.
size: Recorded as vertical cup-to-disc ratio (e.g. 0.7) within a 1 DD disc
how: Draw a second black oval inside the disc circle to mark the cup margin, sized to the vertical C/D ratio; show focal notches as indentations of the rim and write the ratio beside the disc.
src: inferred: black outline for a structural landmark; CMS L33567 App A only asks that optic nerve 'cupping' be recorded, without a colour

refs.title: Diagnosis and pathogenesis of glaucomatous optic neuropathy: morphological aspects.

name: Optic disc hemorrhage (Drance)
def: Splinter- or flame-shaped haemorrhage on or crossing the optic disc margin, a recognised marker of glaucomatous damage and progression.
where: Straddles the disc rim into the peripapillary nerve fibre layer, oriented radially.
how: Draw a short radial red stroke crossing the disc margin at the involved clock hour.
src: CMS L33567 App A

refs.title: Optic disc hemorrhage in glaucoma: pathophysiology and prognostic significance.
Diagnosis and pathogenesis of glaucomatous optic neuropathy: morphological aspects.

name: Optic disc pit
def: Rare congenital circumscribed greyish depression in the optic disc, usually temporal, that may lead to macular schisis and serous macular detachment.
where: Within the disc margin; associated macular fluid extends from the disc toward the fovea.
how: Draw a small black-outlined oval at the temporal disc stippled black to show the grey pit; draw any associated serous macular detachment in blue.
src: inferred: grey depression shown as black stipple; associated detachment blue per CMS L33567 App A

refs.title: Optic disc pit: a review.
Optic disc pit maculopathy: a review of diagnosis and treatment.

name: Optic disc coloboma
def: Congenital excavation of the optic disc from incomplete closure of the embryonic fissure, seen as an enlarged, sharply demarcated, white bowl-shaped defect that is deeper inferiorly.
where: Excavation decentred inferiorly; may be continuous with an inferior chorioretinal coloboma.
how: Enlarge the disc circle inferiorly with a black outline and leave the excavation white; draw any contiguous chorioretinal coloboma with the same code.
src: inferred: white bare excavation with black margin; optic disc anomalies have no standard code (Jayanna S, Shanmugam PM. Indian J Ophthalmol 2022, https://doi.org/10.4103/ijo.IJO_1004_22)

refs.title: Congenital Optic Disc Anomalies: Insights from Multimodal Imaging.

name: Morning glory disc anomaly
def: Congenital funnel-shaped excavation of an enlarged optic disc with a central white glial tuft, a surrounding ring of chorioretinal pigmentary change, and numerous straight vessels radiating from the disc margin.
where: Disc plus a peripapillary ring of pigmentary disturbance; usually unilateral.
size: Enlarged disc with peripapillary ring, larger than 1 DD
how: Draw an enlarged disc with a white centre (glial tuft), a black-stippled peripapillary pigment ring, and many straight red vessels radiating from its edge.
src: inferred: white glial tissue; black = pigment (Retinal diagram, Dr Sabin Sahu, https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/retinal-diagram-dr-sabin-sahu/57240044); red vessels per CMS L33567 App A

refs.title: Update on the morning glory disc anomaly.
Retinal complications associated with congenital optic disc anomalies determined by swept source optical coherence tomography.

name: Optic disc drusen
def: Acellular, often calcified deposits in the prelaminar optic nerve head, visible as refractile yellow-white lumpy bodies when superficial or causing an elevated disc that mimics papilledema when buried.
where: Within the disc substance, giving a lumpy or scalloped margin; frequently bilateral.
size: Small nodules within a 1 DD disc
how: Draw clusters of small yellow circles within the disc circle and give the disc a lumpy, scalloped margin.
src: inferred: drusen are stippled yellow (Documentation & Drawing in Ophthalmology, https://www.eophtha.com/posts/documentation-drawing-in-ophthalmology)

refs.title: Optic disc drusen: a systematic review : Up-to-date and future perspective.
Prevalence of optic disc drusen: A systematic review, meta-analysis and forecasting study.

name: Myelinated retinal nerve fibres
def: Congenital patch of myelinated retinal nerve fibre layer appearing as a white, opaque, feathery-edged patch that follows the nerve fibre pattern and obscures the underlying retinal vessels.
where: Usually contiguous with the disc margin along the arcuate bundles; occasionally an isolated patch elsewhere.
how: Shade a white patch following the arcuate nerve fibre direction, with fine black feathered strokes at its frayed edges; draw vessels within it as interrupted.
src: inferred: natural white colour; no standard code

name: Peripapillary (parapapillary) atrophy
def: Crescent or ring of chorioretinal atrophy adjacent to the optic disc; the beta zone exposes sclera and large choroidal vessels next to the disc margin, and the alpha zone shows irregular hypo/hyperpigmentation outside it.
where: Crescent abutting the disc margin; may encircle the disc in high myopia or glaucoma.
how: Draw a crescent against the (usually temporal) disc margin bounded by a black line: leave the inner beta zone white and stipple the outer alpha zone black for irregular pigment.
src: Retinal diagram, Dr Sabin Sahu, https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/retinal-diagram-dr-sabin-sahu/57240044 (BLACK = RPE, pigment clumping); white bare sclera inferred

refs.title: Beta-Zone parapapillary atrophy and the velocity of glaucoma progression.
Controversies in the association of parapapillary atrophy with glaucoma.

name: Tilted disc
def: Congenital oblique insertion of the optic nerve producing an oval, obliquely oriented disc with an inferonasal crescent, situs inversus of the retinal vessels and inferonasal RPE/choroidal hypoplasia.
where: Oval disc with oblique long axis; crescent and ectatic hypopigmented fundus inferonasally.
how: Draw the disc as an oblique oval with a white, black-outlined crescent at its inferonasal edge; lightly mark any inferonasal ectatic zone.
src: inferred: white bare-sclera crescent with black margin

refs.title: Tilted disc syndrome.
Macular associations of tilted disc syndrome.

name: Optic nerve hypoplasia
def: Congenitally small optic disc with reduced axon number, characteristically surrounded by a peripapillary double-ring sign, often with tortuous retinal vessels and nerve fibre layer thinning.
where: Small disc within a larger scleral-canal ring; unilateral or bilateral.
size: Disc clearly smaller than 1 normal DD
how: Draw a reduced disc circle with a second concentric black ring around it to show the double-ring sign.
src: inferred: black outline for structural landmark

refs.title: Optic nerve hypoplasia.

name: Optic disc melanocytoma
def: Benign, deeply pigmented magnocellular nevus of the optic disc, dark brown to black, often eccentric on the disc and frequently extending into the adjacent choroid or retina.
where: On the disc, often eccentric, overhanging the margin when it has a choroidal (54%) or retinal (30%) component; 99% unilateral.
size: Mean about 2 mm diameter (about 1.3 DD) and 1 mm thick
how: Fill the involved part of the disc solid dark brown with a black outline, extending past the margin where there is a choroidal or retinal component.
src: Retinal diagram, Dr Sabin Sahu, https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/retinal-diagram-dr-sabin-sahu/57240044 (BROWN = melanocytic lesions)

refs.title: Melanocytoma of optic disc in 115 cases: the 2004 Samuel Johnson Memorial Lecture, part 1.

name: Choroidal nevus
def: Benign, well-circumscribed, flat or minimally elevated slate-grey to brown melanocytic choroidal lesion, often with overlying drusen; risk features include thickness >2 mm, subretinal fluid, orange pigment and margin <3 mm from the disc.
where: Mostly postequatorial but can occur anywhere in the choroid.
size: Mean basal diameter about 1.25 mm (about 1 DD) in population studies; giant nevus 10 mm or more; thickness up to 2 mm
how: Fill a flat round or oval patch solid brown; add overlying drusen as yellow dots and any subretinal fluid in blue.
src: CMS L33567 App A

refs.title: Choroidal nevus: a review of prevalence, features, genetics, risks, and outcomes.
Estimating the risk of malignant transformation of a choroidal nevus.

name: Choroidal melanoma
def: Malignant melanocytic tumour of the choroid presenting as an elevated brown dome- or mushroom (collar-button)-shaped mass, often with orange pigment and associated subretinal fluid.
where: Anywhere in the choroid, may extend anteriorly into the ciliary body; frequently with exudative retinal detachment.
size: Thickness: small 0-3 mm, medium 3.1-8 mm, large >8 mm; basal diameter usually several DD
how: Draw a solid brown dome; for a collar-button tumour draw a narrowed waist where it breaks through Bruch membrane; draw associated serous detachment in blue.
src: Documentation & Drawing in Ophthalmology, https://www.eophtha.com/posts/documentation-drawing-in-ophthalmology (BROWN = malignant choroidal melanomas)

Using risk factors for detection and prognostication of uveal melanoma.
[Collar-button choroidal melanoma. Anatomo-radiologic correlations].

name: Amelanotic choroidal melanoma
def: Choroidal melanoma with little or no pigment, appearing as a yellow-tan to pinkish elevated dome or mushroom mass, often with visible intrinsic vessels.
where: Anywhere in the choroid; differential includes metastasis and hemangioma.
size: As for pigmented melanoma (small 0-3 mm, medium 3.1-8 mm, large >8 mm thick)
how: Fill the dome yellow (amelanotic mass) with a brown outline to mark it as a choroidal tumour; draw subretinal fluid in blue.
src: Retinal diagram, Dr Sabin Sahu, https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/retinal-diagram-dr-sabin-sahu/57240044 (YELLOW = amelanotic mass lesions); brown outline = choroidal tumour (Requisites for fundus drawing, https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/retina-drwaing/163697941)

Metastasis of uveal melanoma millimeter-by-millimeter in 8033 consecutive eyes.

name: Circumscribed choroidal hemangioma
def: Benign solitary vascular hamartoma of the choroid presenting as a smooth, orange-red, elevated mass posterior to the equator, frequently with subretinal fluid or cystoid macular edema.
where: Posterior to the equator, commonly macular or juxtapapillary; unilateral and solitary.
size: Usually several DD in basal diameter, a few mm thick
how: Draw a red-filled dome with a brown outline marking its choroidal origin; add overlying serous detachment in blue.
src: Jayanna S, Shanmugam PM. It is time for more colors! Indian J Ophthalmol 2022, https://doi.org/10.4103/ijo.IJO_1004_22 (choroidal vascular tumours such as hemangioma coded red); brown outline = choroidal tumour (https://www.eophtha.com/posts/documentation-drawing-in-ophthalmology)

refs.title: Circumscribed Choroidal Hemangioma.
Circumscribed choroidal hemangioma.

name: Diffuse choroidal hemangioma
def: Diffuse vascular hamartomatous thickening of the choroid, characteristic of Sturge-Weber syndrome, giving a deep red-orange fundus colour and often complicated by exudative retinal detachment.
where: Diffuse, ill-defined, involving much of the posterior choroid of one eye (side of the facial port-wine stain).
size: Extensive, often more than one quadrant
how: Shade the involved fundus red with an ill-defined brown border; draw any exudative detachment in blue.
src: Jayanna S, Shanmugam PM. Indian J Ophthalmol 2022, https://doi.org/10.4103/ijo.IJO_1004_22 (choroidal vascular tumours coded red); brown = choroidal tumour (https://www.eophtha.com/posts/documentation-drawing-in-ophthalmology)

refs.title: Current concepts on diffuse choroidal hemangioma in Sturge Weber syndrome.

name: Bone-spicule pigmentation (retinitis pigmentosa)
def: Intraretinal pigment formed by RPE cells that migrate along retinal vessels after photoreceptor loss; the hallmark mid-peripheral fundus sign of retinitis pigmentosa, usually with attenuated arterioles and waxy disc pallor.
where: Mid-periphery around the equator, sparing the macula until late; spicules outline the retinal capillary network.
size: scattered spicules ~1/10 DD, confluent in a ring
how: Small black branching (spicule-shaped) marks scattered in a ring through the mid-periphery, following the vessels; leave the posterior pole clear.
src: eOphtha drawing convention (black solid = hyperpigmentation / intraretinal pigment); same convention as RPE hyperplasia in this catalogue

name: Stargardt flecks (fundus flavimaculatus)
def: Yellow-white pisciform lipofuscin flecks at the level of the RPE in ABCA4 Stargardt disease, scattered around the macula and posterior pole, often with central atrophy.
where: Posterior pole and around the arcades, sparing the peripapillary ring.
how: Scattered small yellow fish-tail (pisciform) flecks through the posterior pole; add macular atrophy if present.
src: inferred: CMS L33567 App A yellow = exudate/deposits at the level of the RPE (same family as drusen)
